body_text:
A rational number is an equivalence class of pairs $(a,b)$ with
$a\in\mathbb{Z}$ and nonzero $b\in\mathbb{Z}$, where
$(a,b)\sim(c,d)$ exactly when $ad=bc$. The notation $a/b$ names
the class, not a privileged representation; multiplying
numerator and denominator by the same nonzero integer leaves
the rational number unchanged.
